Draws of the expected response

Source: R/posterior_epred.R
posterior_epred.kb_fit.Rd

Draws of the expected response.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'kb_fit'
posterior_epred(
  object,
  new_data = NULL,
  ...,
  new_levels = c("average", "sample"),
  representative_site = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A kb_fit object.

new_data

A data frame with the fit's predictor column (and optional site and year columns), or NULL for the observed data. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is estimated for a site or year not in the data used to fit the model, or when new_data has no site or year column. Sites and years in the model fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "average" (the default): the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

  • "sample": a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. Rows that name the same new site or year, or that have no site or year column, share one effect; give new sites or years different names for independent effects. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

representative_site

A character vector of sites in the fit whose effects a new site adopts (averaged when several are named), or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

Value

A draws-by-observations (D x N) matrix.

Details

Each draw is the expected response, the mean of the fit's likelihood (see kb_model_describe()), given that draw's parameters. For a cover calibration with a presence part, it includes the probability that the plot has plants present. For a Nereocystis weight fit, which is modelled on the log scale, it is the mean weight, not the median.

For draws of new observations, which include residual variation, use posterior_predict().

A site (and optionally year) column in new_data with levels in the fit gives predictions for those levels. With new_data = NULL the observed data is used, with its sites and years.

See also

kb_predict_weight(), which summarises these draws.

Other fit methods: augment.kb_fit(), coef.kb_fit(), fitted.kb_fit(), glance.kb_fit(), kb_model_describe(), kb_samples(), kb_stancode(), log_lik.kb_fit(), posterior_linpred.kb_fit(), posterior_predict.kb_fit(), prior_summary.kb_fit(), residuals.kb_fit(), summary.kb_fit(), tidy.kb_fit()

Examples

ep <- posterior_epred(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
dim(ep)
#> [1] 1500  660
